extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting papers to ICLR 2026 (machine learning/AI community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory policies for preparing and submitting anonymized papers, abstracts, supplementary materials, and related artifacts to the ICLR 2026 conference, including review/revision workflow and author responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract submission deadline and authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must submit paper abstracts by the abstract submission deadline of Sept 19, 2025 AOE. It is key that authors submit genuine and informative abstracts that reflect the content of the full submission, as abstracts will be used in reviewer bidding before the final paper submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placeholder or duplicate abstracts will be removed. Titles and abstracts may be edited before the submission deadline. Author order may be edited after the abstract deadline, but new authors cannot be added. Abstracts submitted by the abstract submission deadline must be genuine; placeholder or duplicate abstracts will be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full paper submission deadline and supplementary materials timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Full paper submissions are due Sept 24, 2025 11:59pm AOE, and the submission site will be open on Sept 13, 2025. Supplementary material is due at the same time as the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deadlines are final and no accommodations can be made for missing them. No edits to the submission can be made after the submission deadline until the release of reviews (except revisions during the allowed discussion period).

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview accounts and author metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must have an OpenReview profile with current information before deadlines. No authors can be added after the abstract submission deadline (author order can be changed until the full paper deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every co-author has an OpenReview profile before the abstract deadline; failure to do so can cause operational issues. If an author used a different email, add and confirm the email to link the submission. For profile merges/contact support, email info@openreview.net.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind anonymity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: ICLR 2026 is double blind: all submitted papers should be anonymous. Any paper where author identity is revealed in either the main text or the supplementary material will be desk rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related arXiv papers by the same authors do not break anonymity; if cited, cite them in third person. Authors can report results on challenge leaderboards, but reviewers are advised not to intentionally search for authors. Maintain anonymity also in supplementary materials and any uploaded links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main text page limit at submission and discussion/camera-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission, the main text should be 9 pages or fewer. During the discussion/rebuttal phase and for the camera ready, the page limit will be increased to 10 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limit will be strictly enforced. Papers with main text beyond the page limit will be desk-rejected. The list of references does not count towards the page limit, and unlimited additional pages are allowed for the bibliography/references. The optional ethics and reproducibility statements do not count toward the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices and reviewers' obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use as many pages of appendices (after the bibliography) as they wish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are not required to read the appendix. Recommended practice: include supplementary text after references (as an appendix) or as a separate supplementary file; for camera-ready it is recommended to include the appendix in the same PDF as the main paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style files and templates requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use the provided LaTeX style files for ICLR 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style files are available at the provided GitHub link (iclr2026.zip). Use them to prepare submissions to ensure formatting compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials and code submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to submit supplementary materials, including source code associated with a paper, as part of the supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code submission helps reviewers assess replicability. Reviewers are encouraged but not required to review supplementary material. Recommended: submit a single file (paper + supplementary text) with supplementary text after references, or include separate files. Make sure supplementary material preserves anonymity when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous code and external demo/link handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can make code or demos available anonymously in several ways (e.g., anonymized zip as supplementary, anonymous repository link, or posting an anonymous link in a comment to reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure host websites do not track visitors (tracking could reveal identity). If link reveals identity or tracks visitors, it may put the submission at risk of rejection. Use methods that keep code visible only to reviewers/ACs if desired (e.g., private anonymous repo + comment to reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Ethics Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to read the ICLR Code of Ethics and are encouraged to include a paragraph Ethics Statement at the end of the main text (before references) if the paper raises ethics questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include human subjects, dataset releases, harmful insights/applications, conflicts of interest, fairness/bias, privacy/security, legal compliance, and research integrity (IRB, documentation). The optional ethics statement will not count toward the page limit but should not be more than 1 page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Reproducibility Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to include a paragraph-long Reproducibility Statement at the end of the main text (before references) to discuss efforts made to ensure reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph should not itself describe the reproduction details but should reference parts of the main paper, appendix, and supplemental material that enable reproduction (e.g., code links, proofs, dataset processing). The reproducibility statement is not part of the main text and does not count toward the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewing requirement (author-reviewer obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who are on 3 or more papers must serve as a reviewer for at least 6 papers. All submissions must have at least one author who is registered to review at least 3 papers (and be qualified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors in the '3 or more papers' category who fail to finish reviews by rebuttal stage may have their papers desk rejected. Qualification: at least one accepted publication at a previous ICLR/NeurIPS/ICML or equivalent journal. If none qualify, they are exempt. Program chairs may grant exceptions case-by-case. Authors will be notified to register as reviewers after the abstract deadline; if none of the authors are registered as a reviewer, it will result in desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission and prior-publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions identical (or substantially similar) to versions previously published, accepted for publication, or submitted in parallel to other conferences/journals are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers on non-peer-reviewed websites (like arXiv) or presented at non-archival workshops do not violate the policy. Submission to archival repositories such as arXiv is allowed during the review period. The policy is enforced throughout the reviewing process. OpenReview provides anonymous BibTeX entries to allow citation of papers under review without revealing authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Large Language Models (LLMs) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of LLMs is allowed as a general-purpose assist tool. If LLMs played a significant role in research ideation and/or writing to the extent that they could be regarded as a contributor, authors should describe the precise role of the LLM in a separate section on LLM usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The LLM usage section can appear in the appendix and will not count as part of the page limit. Not disclosing significant LLM usage can lead to desk rejection. Authors take full responsibility for content written under their name, including content generated by LLMs that could be construed as plagiarism or fabrication. LLMs are not eligible for authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy and archival nature of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may withdraw papers at any time until decisions have been announced. Before the paper submission deadline, withdrawing deletes the paper from OpenReview; after the submission deadline, withdrawn papers remain hosted publicly and will be de-anonymized immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers submitted are considered archival for scientific purposes and cannot be deleted. Withdrawn papers will be visible in the 'withdrawn papers' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing process: public reviews, discussion, and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: ICLR uses a reviewing workflow with official (anonymous, public) reviews, a public discussion period, private reviewer/AC discussion, and final decisions. Key dates: reviews released Nov 11; public discussion Nov 11–Dec 3; private discussion Dec 3–Jan 22; decisions on Jan 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can post responses to reviews during public discussion and revise papers until Dec 3; OpenReview will apply a pdfdiff to compare revisions to the original. Area chairs and reviewers may ignore changes that are significantly different from the original paper. All submitted papers (accepted, rejected or withdrawn) will be deanonymized after notification; reviews and comments will be released publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public discussion norms and comment visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview allows public discussion during the discussion phase. Anybody logged in can post comments that are publicly visible, or restrict visibility to reviewers and up, ACs and up, or just PCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments apart from those of the authors, reviewers, ACs or the organizing committee will be required to be non-anonymous. Authors may post multiple replies to each reviewer; there is a word limit per comment but no limit on the number of comments. Be civil and considerate of reviewers' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and rules on editing submissions after deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions can be edited on OpenReview until the submission deadline (Sept 24). After that, edits are not allowed until reviews are released, except authors may revise during the public discussion period (Nov 11–Dec 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No edits to submitted papers can be made after the submission deadline except via the allowed discussion-period revisions; authors cannot request individual exceptions. If a revision is made during discussion, a pdfdiff is applied and significant changes may be ignored by reviewers/ACs. Title and abstract can be revised for the full paper submission so long as the revised version stays close to the original abstract; otherwise the paper may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready and presentation logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera-ready instructions will be emailed mid-February 2026. The page limit for camera-ready is identical to the submission version (10 pages). At least one author must register for 'Conference and Workshops' (student registration allowed for students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who registered to attend in-person and offered an oral spot will present in person. Registered authors will record a 5-minute summary video; all videos will be hosted on iclr.cc. Accepted papers receive a SlidesLive recording link. Poster sessions are in-person only (no virtual poster session this year). Spotlight papers are specially recognized on posterboards. Author order can be updated for camera ready but authors cannot be added or removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for noncompliance (desk rejection risks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain policy violations may lead to desk rejection or other penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: revealing author identity in text/supplementary or failing to register a required reviewer can cause desk rejection; submitting placeholder abstracts will be deleted; not finishing required reciprocal reviews by rebuttal stage may cause desk rejection; not disclosing significant LLM usage can lead to desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for handling de-anonymization concerns (challenge results etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submitted paper refers to a challenge they won which can identify the authors, it is acceptable to report results on the leaderboard and include the ranking and challenge name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are advised to not intentionally search authors by examining leaderboards. If authors encounter potential Code of Ethics violations during review/public discussion, raise issues privately to the paper's Area Chair via OpenReview.
